recipes.name: Torsk (Scandinavian Cod)
ingredients_raw: 6 cups water, or more as needed

steps.text: Preheat the broiler. Lightly grease a cookie sheet.

Mix together water, sugar, and salt in a large saucepan. Add fillets to water mixture; add more water to fully submerge fillets if needed. Bring water to a boil over medium-high heat. Boil for 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove fillets from water and blot dry on paper towels. Brush with 6 tablespoons melted butter; sprinkle with paprika.
Broil in the preheated broiler until fillets are golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes per inch of thickness. Serve with remaining melted butter.

raw_recipe.headline: Torsk (Scandinavian Cod)
raw_recipe.description: Torsk is a Scandinavian dish of poached and broiled cod with butter. You can use frozen cod; defrosting is not necessary.

review.reviewBody: Awesome, entire family loved it! The only thing I did different was adding only 1/2 cup splenda instead of 1 cup sugar to the water. Plus - I don't think you need quite as much butter, I only used 3 tbsps while broiling.

For My Own Notes: 1 filet, 3 cups water, 2 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt. Cover filet completely. Set to Medium High. Bring to a boil. Set timer for 2 mins. Set atop broiler pan, broil low 6 mins, then high for 2 mins.

Nice way to use frozen cod. Served it with mashed potatoes and the whole family loved it, even the young kids. After seeing reviews about it being bland, I added some extra salt to the melted butter before brushing it on. And I really slathered those fillets up, did not hold back. The broil time was less than indicated for me, so I'd suggest checking it after the first 4 minutes. Mine was done in about 6. I also suggest brushing a bit more butter on as soon as it comes out of the oven. Really tasty and, yes, slightly reminiscent of broiled lobster. Adding this to my rotation.

We loved this - we used cod fillets that were a little on the thin side. I did not boil them, I just brought them up to simmer till they were opaque and then took them out. After patting them dry I gave them a little shmear of garlic paste, then drizzled with butter and sprinkled with seafood seasoning. Broiling was shorter because they were thin, and they turned out awesome! Delicious! The family loved it, thanks for the recipe!

As advertised - easy and tastes (kind of) like lobster. However, I'd say this could easily work with less butter. I used only the 6 tablespoons it calls for as basting liquid - putting about 3/4 of it on prior to broiling, and the rest after broiling before serving, and I thought it was still too much. No need to add extra butter tableside. Best parts of the recipe are that it's prepared from frozen and it loses its fishy taste in the sweet boiling liquid and the buttery broil, to appease picky eaters who don't like fish.

Kudos to the author of the recipe - it really does taste somewhat like lobster! I appreciated not having to defrost the fish to make this recipe. Especially on a weeknight. On the first go-around: (1) I halved the butter and sugar amount (2) used homemade chicken broth (3) did not use foil. Next time, I will most likely cut down the butter and sugar by 1/3 or 1/4 to make it a bit healthier. Cooking it in the broth made it taste extra flavorful. And I think not using the foil resulted in a slightly drier fish.

This does have the texture of lobster tail and it has a taste similar to it as well. I assume it's from the first step of boiling in salt and sugar water. ( I did this in the morning to make dinner more quickly) I then dried and chilled it until dinnertime. My husband LOVED it! And he usually likes fried fish:) So, I would make this again, but probably not all the time as I think it's probably not as healthy as plain broiled cod with pepper and lime juice. I did use a little less butter than called for and it was plenty-(I used a half stick) we even had some leftover. (we also added garlic to the butter)

Great recipe. It does taste very similar to lobster. You don't even need to broil the fish. Instead of broiling, I melted 2-3 tbs of butter in the pan over medium-low heat and cooked the cod on both sides until it was slightly golden brown, adding paprika to one side. I also used Splenda instead of sugar in the water mix.

I used cod loins and followed the directions without alterations. The fish's texture was lovely and firm, and I appreciated how the sugar/salt subtly amped up the flavor of the fish itself. However, it wasn't enough flavor, and the fish was really bland. I would make this again, but I'll double the salt and add some whole aromatics to the simmering liquid with the fish - maybe some garlic, shallot, and I bet dill and/or tarragon would be nice. I also found that I used about half the butter than the recipe called for, but I think it's because I used loins rather than fillets.

Just to clear something up: "torsk" is simply the Norwegian word for cod. It has nothing to do with whether it's prepared with paprika and butter, it's just a word. Having said that, I have made torsk many different ways and this method was a winner. I had a little problem with the fillets coming apart in the water, so next time I have to boil more gently, but the taste was still very good. I would make it this way again.

Try this twice. Both times I use frozen cod loins instead of fillets. First time followed as written we really liked it but it was missing something. The second time I add garlic, salt, pepper, and dill to the butter . I also followed tip from previous review to refrigerate after boiling. I also flipped the loins over half way through broiling . It was wonderful , no leftovers.
The only thing I did differently is add capers to the butter.

This a good recipe for the cod. The improvement would be to serve with peas and boiled potatoes (chunks) with melted butter on the side for dipping both the cod and potatoes. Then you have reached cod nirvana.
I’ve never before heard of this so there’s a learning curve for me. I think it’s quite good adding things to your preferences and decreasing sugar. Remember: most frozen cod here is 4oz fillets!

I make this often with no changes to the recipe. My husband and I consider it our "poor man's lobster". I've given out the recipe to family and friends as no one can believe how easy it is prepare and how great it tastes. This is a terrific way to serve cod. I think it's funny that our grocery store labels the cod "Torsk". Scandinavian Minnesota...this is the only way to make cod!

So delicious and it was simple to make. I did boil my filets separately for about 3-4min rather than all of them at once. Everyone in the family loved it to the point were there were no leftovers going in the fridge.

For me this just tasted like fish with sugar. Many years ago there was a recipe that made the rounds for using monkfish and some seasonings and caraway seeds which was excellent. Unfortunately I lost it and haven’t been able to find anything like it in the years since. At least I was only feeding myself and not anybody else
My better half loved it but I found it to sweet even after cutting the sugar by half

Really enjoyed this! The only thing I did was take the suggestion of putting it in the fridge after boiling. Made it with a side of brown rice and mascarpone cauliflower mashers. The flavors I used just melded well together with this recipe.
